clue.text: Meat done, butter pie's filling

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, like a ram

indicators.note: a pie's filling is what sits in its middle, so take the centre letter of PIE

explanation.surface: A cook reporting that the meat is cooked and the butter has gone into the pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is pronounced as the dairy spread in the surface, but here it is one who butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: this cured, smoked beef is one kind of meat.

clue.text: Rocky Balboa primarily ran after training

indicators.note: primarily = in the first place, so take the first letter of Balboa

explanation.surface: The boxer Rocky Balboa going for a run as part of his training montage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the film boxer's first name; it is the adjective that defines the answer, and Balboa only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground strewn with small stones is stony, so rocky.

clue.text: Maybe salt settled unknown hotelier's concern?

parts.note: to salt food is one way to season it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a mystery hotelier's worry is simply the salt on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is an example: a hotel's trade rises and falls with the tourist calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the swing between busy and quiet times of year is what worries someone running a hotel.

clue.text: Go on about setter in peak form?

parts.note: to go on a horse or bus is to ride it

explanation.surface: Urging a crossword setter to keep talking while at the top of their game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts you towards the usual I or ME for the compiler; here it is something that sets hair. The question mark covers the pun on 'peak form'.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description: the line running along a row of summits is a shape made of peaks.

clue.text: Trite manifestos irritated parliamentary assistant?

indicators.note: letters that are irritated are stirred up and put out of order

explanation.surface: A political aide annoyed by the stale party manifestos.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK this is a middle-rank minister who helps the Secretary of State run a department; the question mark flags the loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose gloss: the post is a junior one, supporting the Cabinet minister in charge.

clue.text: Country band drink, losing heads

indicators.note: both words lose their first letter, their head

parts.note: GANG, a band, without its first letter
COLA, a drink, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A country-music band drinking until they are out of their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country band' reads as a single idea, a group playing country music; the definition is 'Country' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the nations of southern Africa.

clue.text: Late sleeper close to windfall on vacation

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: WINDFALL emptied to its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone who sleeps in on holiday after coming into some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as one phrase meaning near; here the two words work separately, and the definition asks for a person, not a time.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone who habitually stays up into the small hours goes to bed late.

clue.text: Pretentiously huge shelter layout is reworked

indicators.note: the letters of LAYOUT IS are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Showing off with an absurdly large marquee that keeps being redesigned.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the clothing size for outsize, a crossword staple for 'huge'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe doing something showily, to impress.

clue.text: Bow man getting bronzed before function

parts.note: a bow is curved like an arc

explanation.surface: An archer getting a suntan before going to a social function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow man' reads as one archer, and 'function' as a party; the answer is from trigonometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the inverse of the tangent is one of the trigonometric functions.

clue.text: Lift up and incline inverted section of plane

parts.note: to cock a hat or an ear is to tilt it up

indicators.note: inverted means turned the other way

explanation.surface: Instructions for raising and tilting part of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' is the aircraft here, not the geometric flat surface that 'incline' and 'section' suggest.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the pilots' compartment at the front is one part of an aircraft.

clue.text: Hold criminal you shouldn't have inside

parts.note: what you say on getting a gift: ta, thanks

explanation.surface: A jailer holding a convict who ought not to be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' reads as a reproach; it is the polite thanks for a present, and TA is British informal for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a jug that holds a litre has room for that much inside it.

clue.text: Stop county introducing combat sport

indicators.note: the county comes first and brings in the sport after it

explanation.surface: A county council trying to ban a new cage-fighting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' reads as a command; in punctuation the stops are the marks that pause a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An old printing sense: punctuation marks are called stops, and this is the one for a short pause.

clue.text: Emergency device deployed taco, pint, and bun

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and set up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A safety gadget set off by a taco, a pint of beer and a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' before 'bun' joins the last item to the fodder list; all three foods are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: it is the switch pressed to raise the alarm in a crisis.

clue.text: Burlesque tango party somewhere filthy

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO alphabet
a pigsty is a filthy place

explanation.surface: A raunchy show with tango dancing at a party held in a dive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burlesque' suggests a striptease show; here it is the older sense, a mocking imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean a grotesque, mocking imitation.

clue.text: Clumsy boat, advanced horn

parts.note: an old tub is a slow, awkward boat
A = advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A lumbering boat moving forward and sounding its foghorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horn' reads as a ship's foghorn beside 'boat'; it is a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose usage: brass instruments are colloquially called horns, and this is the deepest of them.

clue.text: Kind nurse eats around German state

parts.note: a brand is a kind or make

indicators.note: around means turned about

explanation.surface: A gentle nurse having a meal while travelling in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' reads as gentle and 'eats' as a verb; they are a noun meaning type and a noun meaning food.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of Germany's sixteen Länder, the one surrounding Berlin.

clue.text: What tinkering with machine a ton may reveal?

definitions.text: What tinkering with machine a ton may reveal?

indicators.note: to tinker with something is to fiddle about with its parts

explanation.surface: Someone who tinkers with machines all the time, showing their obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: fiddling with machinery a lot betrays an obsession with technology. 'A ton' means a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: endless fiddling with gadgets betrays an obsessive enthusiasm for technology.

clue.text: Fail to keep love free

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: to fail in a contest is to lose
love = zero, O in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A lament about failing to cling to a love that ought to be set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score of zero, which looks like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an animal running loose is at liberty.

clue.text: Groom small mammal

parts.note: the marten is a weasel-like mammal

explanation.surface: Grooming the fur of a little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' reads as brushing an animal's coat; it is the verb for tidying oneself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to groom yourself is to make yourself neat and tidy.

clue.text: Fall volcanic output turning a new red

indicators.note: turning means going round to face the other way

parts.note: lava pours out of a volcano
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, a Red

explanation.surface: Lava flowing down the slope and glowing a fresh red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' reads as a colour of lava; it is a communist, and Che Guevara is the crossword's usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: A specific sense: a sudden slide of snow down a mountain is a fall.

clue.text: Record regularly spun to help wake up

indicators.note: something spun is turned round

parts.note: to rise is to get up after waking

explanation.surface: A record played on the turntable every morning as an alarm call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record regularly spun' reads as a vinyl disc on repeat; 'regularly' belongs with 'Record' in the definition and 'spun' works on 'help'.
explanation.definitionFit: A precise gloss: putting engagements in a diary is writing them down day after day.

clue.text: Might this be rightful gain, won freely?

definitions.text: Might this be rightful gain, won freely?

indicators.note: the letters move freely into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking whether an easy prize won without effort is fairly earned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the phrase means a reward won easily, without a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: the idiom names easy gains, won with little effort, and the clue asks whether such gains are deserved.

clue.text: Extra large farewell, hugging perhaps

explanation.surface: A big goodbye with a hug thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat; this one is taken after the ball hits the batter's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket sense: runs not scored off the bat are extras, and this is the one from the ball striking the batter's body.

clue.text: Fruit almost deserving of plant

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so WORTH falls one letter short

parts.note: WORTH, deserving, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A fruit that is nearly worthy of the plant it grows on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserving of' reads as a phrase; 'of' is only the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a flowering plant of the genus Scrophularia.

clue.text: Pretty adequate, I agree

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict: it will do, and I won't argue.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits a single lukewarm remark into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one phrase: reasonable enough in quality, and a spoken concession of someone's point.

clue.text: Skin treatment formula emptied, spies bottom of vial

indicators.note: FORMULA emptied of its insides leaves F and A

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A spy noticing the dregs at the bottom of an empty bottle of skin cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formula' suggests a beauty product's recipe; only its first and last letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a cleansing, moisturising session for the face is a beauty treatment.

clue.text: Struggle with name adopted by North American capital

parts.note: to vie is to struggle, compete

explanation.surface: An immigrant struggling with a new name after moving to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is a city; the surface points to America, but the answer is in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Where you won't find favour overseas?

definitions.text: Where you won't find favour overseas?

parts.note: the surface means a place where you are unpopular; the setter means the word 'favour' itself, as spelt
across the Atlantic the word is spelt without the U, so the place is a variety of the language

explanation.surface: Someone who is unpopular abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' reads as goodwill; it is the word itself, spelt with a U in Britain but without it across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: A spelling joke: in US usage the word is written 'favor', so the British 'favour' is absent there.

clue.text: Secured husband with brooding aesthetic

explanation.surface: Landing a husband who has a moody, artistic look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brooding aesthetic' reads as a description of the husband; it defines a dark style of dress and music.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the black-clad, gloomy fashion and music style is a brooding look.

clue.text: Smashing piece, yet vocals need to transcend atmosphere

indicators.note: the letters are smashed and pieced together again

explanation.surface: A music review: a terrific track, but the singing needs to rise above the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' reads as British praise for the piece and 'atmosphere' as its mood; one is the instruction and the other is Earth's air.
explanation.definitionFit: A precise gloss: it is the speed a rocket needs to break free of Earth's gravity and leave the air behind.

clue.text: One tantalising puzzle

definitions.meaning: a problem that taxes the brain

explanation.surface: A single baffling conundrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One tantalising puzzle' reads as a single phrase; it splits into a person who teases and a brain-teaser.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who teases and tantalises, and a tricky problem.

clue.text: Witch endures through repeatedly taking years to show grief

parts.note: a crone is an old witch
to see out a storm is to endure through it

explanation.surface: An old witch who has lived through many years of hardship and grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' is the key: the letter for years is used twice, inserted into each of the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: weeping uncontrollably is how the phrase shows grief.

clue.text: Wife escapes in a brawl shaking salon

indicators.note: the remaining letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: W = wife, the letter that leaves
IN A BRAWL without W, anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A wife slipping away from a fight that is rocking the beauty parlour.
explanation.walkthrough: The W removed from IN A BRAWL leaves seven letters, which the anagram rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a shop offering manicures is a kind of salon.

clue.text: Rubbish snow leopard at back of its habitat

indicators.note: at the back of means behind

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: Litter found at the back of a snow leopard's lair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as a noun, litter; it is the verb meaning criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang sense: to rubbish an idea is to condemn it publicly.

clue.text: Tear into present for riding gear

parts.note: present at = at, as in 'at home'
tack is a horse's saddle and bridle

explanation.surface: Ripping open a gift of riding equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear into present' reads as unwrapping a gift; the definition is 'Tear into' and 'present' gives a two-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to tear into someone is to assault them, verbally or physically.

clue.text: Main opponent surrendering first of records

indicators.note: to surrender is to give up, so RIVAL gives up its first letter

parts.note: arch = chief, main, as in arch-enemy
RIVAL, an opponent, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A chief rival giving up the first of several records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main opponent' suggests ARCH-RIVAL whole, and 'first of records' seems to remove an R; but 'of records' is the definition and 'surrendering first' works on 'opponent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: archives are stores of records, so the adjective means relating to them.

clue.text: Metal trolley holding elevated highbrow fish

explanation.surface: A supermarket trolley carrying a posh fish raised high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' in a down clue means read upwards; 'highbrow' is a noun here, an intellectual who looks down on others.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: steel whose main added element is carbon is a metal.

clue.text: Dance time at work put a strain on her?

definitions.text: Dance time at work put a strain on her?

parts.note: not a dancer's shift but rehearsal, the working hours of a dance company
the surface makes her the one strained; she is the one who works the dancers hard

explanation.surface: A dancer finding that too many working hours of dancing has worn her out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a woman strained by her job; turned round, she is the one who puts dancers through the strain of rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the woman who rehearses a ballet company works the dancers hard.

clue.text: Element of genius associated with relativity?

definitions.text: Element of genius associated with relativity?

parts.note: not an ingredient of brilliance but a chemical element named after a genius
the genius is the physicist who devised the theory of relativity

explanation.surface: Asking what quality of a great mind lies behind the theory of relativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Element of genius' reads as an ingredient of brilliance; it is a chemical element named for the genius behind relativity.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: element 99 is named after Albert Einstein, the genius behind relativity.

clue.text: Father cycled, bearing struggle

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father who cycles while carrying a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycled' reads as riding a bike; it tells you to rotate the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: opposing a force or power is a struggle against it.

clue.text: Catch yak eating another's tail

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater

parts.note: to yak is to chatter, gab

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A yak caught chewing the tail of another animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yak' reads as the shaggy ox; it is the verb for chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to seize something suddenly is to catch it.

clue.text: In Madrid, the true football team?

parts.note: true = even, level, as in a true surface

explanation.surface: Asking whether Real Madrid is the one genuine football club.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Real Madrid, 'real' meaning true; 'In Madrid' just says to put 'the' into Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: A football sense: a side of that many players is called by its number.

clue.text: Runner who improves famous body in bath?

parts.note: the French revolutionary Marat was murdered in his bath
a honer sharpens, improving an edge

explanation.surface: A runner soaking in the bath to improve their physique.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was stabbed in his bath in 1793, a scene famous from David's painting 'The Death of Marat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one who runs 26-mile races is a runner.

clue.text: Warning curtailed difficult person on bender

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, literally with the tail cut off, so HARD loses its last letter

parts.note: a binger is someone on a drinking spree

explanation.surface: A warning about a troublesome drunk out on a binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult person' reads as one phrase, a nuisance, but the words split across two pieces; a bender is British slang for a drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a forerunner of something coming serves as a warning of it.

clue.text: Extravagant drinks dispenser saves time

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside

parts.note: an optic is the upside-down bottle measure behind a British bar
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A lavish bar gadget that pours drinks quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is a British pub fitting that dispenses a measured shot of spirits from an inverted bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: behaviour like grand opera is over the top, extravagant.

clue.text: Good bit of cricket, and not official

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket

explanation.surface: Praising a spell of cricket that was not officially sanctioned.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six deliveries from one bowler; 'official' reads as an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the person in charge of a state, prison or school board is an official.

clue.text: Sort of music stream carries brute through depression

parts.note: a pock is a small pit in a surface
an ogress is a female ogre, a brute

explanation.surface: A stream carrying some beast along through a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, one inside the other; a pock is a small pit in the skin, as in a pockmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 1970s rock genre of long, complex pieces is a sort of music.

clue.text: Shiny decoration to cover most of valley

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: to span a distance is to cover it
GLEN, a valley, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Glitter spread over most of a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A glen is a Scottish word for a narrow valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: a small glittering disc sewn onto clothing is a shiny decoration.

clue.text: Slip object in trumpet, taking arrangement in wrong direction

indicators.note: taking means taking in, holding
the whole is then written backwards

parts.note: a mute is pushed into a trumpet's bell to soften it

explanation.surface: Dropping something into a trumpet while playing an arrangement backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces come from music: the mute for a trumpet, and 'arr.' as printed on a score before the arranger's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a printed error, listed in a book's corrections, is a slip.

clue.text: Cream to finish uncle's tossed salad

indicators.note: tossed like salad leaves, the letters are mixed
the finishing letter of CREAM

explanation.surface: A cream dressing to finish off an uncle's salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossed' is doubly apt: it is what you do to a salad and the instruction to mix the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a mix of young leaves from Provence is a salad.

clue.text: Concerned with arbitrary leader and tense attendant

parts.note: a sultan rules by his own will

explanation.surface: A nervous servant waiting on a despotic ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attendant' reads as a servant; it is the adjective meaning that goes along with, as in attendant risks.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives describe what follows from or accompanies something.

clue.text: Hardly straight down?

definitions.meaning: a liar is not straight, honest

explanation.surface: A remark that something is not exactly vertical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Straight down' reads as vertical; split, 'hardly straight' means dishonest and 'down' means horizontal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: telling untruths, so hardly straight, and stretched out flat, so down.

clue.text: Cracking old composition reduced by a note

parts.note: n. = note, as in footnote references

explanation.surface: An old piece of music that is superb even with a note cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as British praise, meaning excellent; it is the verb, as in cracking open a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cracking a safe or a bottle is getting it open.

clue.text: Shred portion of studio tapes

indicators.note: the answer is a portion of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Destroying some of a recording studio's tapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shred' reads as a verb, to tear up tapes; it is the noun, a tiny scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the smallest Greek letter came to mean the tiniest amount.

clue.text: Those climbing in vain, else regularly falling

indicators.note: every other letter falls away, leaving the rest

parts.note: the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of IN VAIN ELSE

explanation.surface: Mountaineers striving in vain while others keep falling off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those climbing' pictures mountaineers; the climbers are plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: these evergreen plants climb walls and trees.

clue.text: Musical family assuming agent hid broadcast

indicators.note: the letters of AGENT HID are scattered

explanation.surface: A family taking in a secret agent who had hidden from the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' reads as describing the family; it is the definition, a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Rodgers and Hammerstein show about the King of Siam is a musical.

clue.text: London area bar opening, tying up hotel badly

indicators.note: bar = except, so everything except the opening letter

parts.note: KNOTTING, tying up, without its first letter
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Tying up a bar near a badly run hotel in west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar opening' reads as a pub opening its doors; 'bar' means except, so the opening letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a district of west London famous for its carnival.

clue.text: Scent case of negligence on company register

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: a log is a register or record

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across answer

explanation.surface: A company register records a case of negligence involving perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of negligence' reads as a legal claim; 'case' asks only for the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gloss: toilet water named after the German city became the general word for a light scent.

clue.text: Noted misery at intervals in every journey

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of EVERY JOURNEY

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable on and off during every trip you take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misery' is a person here: British English calls a gloomy person a misery, and the answer is the downcast donkey from A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A British sense: a misery is a gloomy person, and Milne's donkey is the most famous one.

clue.text: Instrument in that place just short of pit

indicators.note: just short means only one letter short, so MINE loses its last letter

parts.note: MINE, a pit, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A tool left in some spot just before the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' reads as a tool; it is an electronic musical instrument played without touching it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the electronic instrument played by moving hands near its aerials is a musical instrument.
